youtube.title: Marie Antoinette Never Said "Let Them Eat Cake"
youtube.description:
The famous line comes from Jean-Jacques Rousseau's Confessions, whose first six books were written around 1765, when Marie Antoinette was nine and still in Austria. Rousseau attributed "Qu'ils mangent de la brioche" (let them eat brioche) to an unnamed "great princess", and may have invented the anecdote. There is no evidence Marie Antoinette ever said it; the line was attached to her long after her death.

📂 Case File #061: Let Them Eat Cake
